headline: US October Payrolls Rise by 165,000 as Unemployment Rate Dips to 4.1%
summary: The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, with the unemployment rate falling to 4.1%. The figures exceeded market expectations, following an upwardly revised gain of 60,000 jobs in September.
why: US employment data is a primary indicator of economic health, heavily influencing Federal Reserve interest rate policy and market sentiment regarding inflation and growth.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Stronger-than-expected job growth suggests economic resilience.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Stronger labor market data often leads to higher Treasury yields as investors price in a more hawkish Federal Reserve stance to prevent overheating.
